Subject: High latency + 5xx spike on api.redwood.stellarnet — urgent

Hi Olga,

We started seeing a large latency spike and an uptick in 5xx errors hitting the Redwood inference endpoint (api.redwood.stellarnet) at ~15:25 UTC. Client throughput dropped by ~30% and several requests returned 502/504. Our SREs are isolating traffic, but this is impacting billing page generation and downstream product tests.

Can you confirm whether this is a regional capacity issue or a software regression? We're tracking this as Sev 2 on our side; any ETA to stabilize would be appreciated.

Attaching a sample of failing request IDs: see error-samples.txt.

Thanks,
Carlos Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, Stellarnet

Quick triage update (notes from the runtime team):

- Timeline: spike started ~2027-07-20T15:24Z; mitigations applied 15:40Z reduced error rate but latency remained elevated until 16:05Z.
- Symptoms: transient KV cache thrashing on the dedicated pool supporting Stellarnet (pool-id dcap-05), leading to backend threads blocking and request retries surfacing as 502/504.
- Root cause hypothesis: an unusually high burst of long-sequence requests triggered a fallback path that forced synchronous KV checkpointing during a window when autoscaler was concurrently reclaiming idle workers. The combination exposed a race between checkpoint I/O and worker lifecycle.

Evidence & artifacts attached:
- threshold-spike-logs.zip (serving logs + kernel traces) [attachment]
- error-samples.txt (from customer) [attachment]

Immediate mitigations we applied:
1) Disabled synchronous checkpointing for reusable KV entries on the pool (config flag: kv.checkpoint.sync=false) — reduced blocking.
2) Temporarily pinned Stellarnet routes to extra burst capacity nodes (dcap-05-burst) to increase headroom.
3) Raised per-route connection limits and blocked a small subset of heavy backtest jobs identified by request signatures.

Proposed corrective actions (short/medium term) and owners:
- Short (24-72h): refine checkpoint gating to prefer async flush when load > 60% (owner: rishi.malhotra), increase autoscaler cooldown to prevent worker churn during spikes (owner: laura.bennett).
- Medium (2–4 weeks): implement per-route read/write KV quotas and introduce a fast-path bypass for long-sequence inference (owner: runtime infra team / Rishi).
- Long (Q3): add canary+chaos tests that simulate long-sequence bursts against dedicated pools (owner: hq-qa / marissa_cole).

Next steps: I'll assemble a short RCA slide deck for exec readout and customer delivery.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Carlos / Amelia — attaching a concise RCA + remediation commitments for your review. High-level executive summary below.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-07-20T15:24Z — 2027-07-20T16:05Z.
- Impact: transient 5xx increase (peak 12% of requests) and median latency increase from 180ms -> 760ms for affected routes. Throughput reduced ~30% for a subset of heavy-sequence flows.
- Root cause: KV checkpointing race combined with aggressive autoscaler lifecycle during long-sequence bursts on a dedicated pool.
- Immediate mitigations: async checkpoint toggle, temporary route pinning to burst nodes, job-blocking for identified heavy signatures.

Committed actions and owners (summary):
- Rishi: gating logic for checkpointing + production patch to default to async when CPU > 60% (ETA 48h).
- Laura: coordinate customer-facing status updates and verify mitigations (ongoing until closure).
- Marissa: design chaos tests for long-sequence bursts and run in staging (ETA 3 weeks).
- Vivek: approve one-time credit to Stellarnet for the impacted billing window and sign off on SLA exception (executive).

Attachments: rca-slide-deck.pdf (2-slide exec summary + action register), threshold-spike-logs.zip, error-samples.txt.

Please confirm receipt and whether you want a short exec call tomorrow for a live walkthrough.

Olga Petrov

Carlos
